title: Native result
description: What one application did with one OPF-exported .pptx file: the files/<fileId>/result.json of a native run directory. Every driver (Keynote, PowerPoint, Impress) writes this same shape; scripts/native-acceptance/core/result/README.md explains it.

schemaVersion.description: The version of this format. Always 1.

deck.description: The deck the file was exported from, lower case (for example "slide-links").

variant.description: Which export of the deck: "default" when the deck has one export only, else the export's name (for example "native", "static").

path.description: The file's path relative to the run's input root, with forward slashes. Never absolute.

sha256.description: Lower-case hex SHA-256 of the input file, read before the application opened it.

unchangedAfterRun.description: True when the file's SHA-256 after the run equals the one before (the application did not save over it); null when it was not checked.

started.description: When the driver began work on this file, UTC (for example "2026-11-25T17:15:25Z").

finished.description: When the driver finished work on this file, UTC.

verbs.description: One entry per verb the driver implements. Every key is required: a verb that did not run says "not-run".

open.description: Opening the file. "done" means it opened without an error; whether a repair prompt appeared is established only by a driver that can see the application's dialogs (one that cannot says so in message).

slideCount.description: How many slides the application says the opened file has, hidden slides counted.

warnings.description: The application's own import warnings, word for word.

status.description: "read": the whole list was read (an empty lines means the application reported none). "partial": some lines were read and the list was cut off. "not-read": the warnings could not be read (for example Keynote shows its Warnings window only while it is in front).

source.description: Where the lines came from: "application" (its scripting interface), "screen" (text recognized in a capture of its window), "log" (a log file it wrote); null when nothing was captured.

lines.description: One entry per warning, in the application's order.

text.description: The warning as the application wrote it (for example "The font Roboto is missing. Your text might look different.").

slides.description: The slide numbers the application names for this warning (Keynote: a "Slide(s) 4" line under it).

layouts.description: The slide layout names the application names for this warning (Keynote: a "Slide Layout(s): Cover, Gallery" line under it).

render.description: The application's own picture of every slide, written as slides/slide-001.png and so on.

pixelSize.description: [width, height] of the pictures in pixels.

colorProfile.description: The ICC profile embedded in the pictures, by its description (Keynote: "Display P3").

alpha.description: True when the pictures have an alpha channel.

probe.description: Reading the object list of every slide through the application's scripting interface.

resave.description: The application's own PowerPoint copy of the opened file (resaved.pptx), then closing the file without saving it.

path.description: The copy's path relative to this result.json's folder, normally "resaved.pptx".

edits.description: Optional edit cases: per case the driver made one edit to the opened file in the application, wrote one PowerPoint copy of it with the application's own writer (edits/<id>.pptx) and left the opened file unsaved. resave keeps the unedited copy. Absent when the driver made no edits.

slides.description: Every slide of the opened file in file order, hidden slides included. Empty when neither render nor probe ran.

details.description: Target-specific facts about the file as the application opened it (for example the fonts it reports for the presentation, the slide size). No shared code reads it.

target.description: The application under test: "keynote" (Keynote on macOS), "powerpoint" (PowerPoint on Windows), "impress" (LibreOffice Impress), "powerpoint-mac" (PowerPoint on macOS).

application.description: The application as it reports itself. Read from the application at run time, never hard-coded.

build.description: Its build number when known (for example "7052.0.68").

system.description: The operating system the application ran on.

fonts.description: Which fonts the application could use: "installed" (whatever the machine has), or a named font profile (Impress: "opf", "stock").

opf.description: The OPF that exported the input.

commit.description: The git commit it was built from, when it was not a published release.

fileId.description: <deck>~<variant>, lower case, characters a-z 0-9 . _ - and one ~. Names the file's folder under files/.

relativePath.description: A relative path with forward slashes: no leading slash, no drive letter, no backslash, no .. segment.

verbStatus.description: "done": the verb finished without an error. "failed": the application returned an error. "timeout": it did not answer in time (a driver without screen access also reports a modal prompt it cannot see this way). "alert": an unexpected dialog or window appeared (captured, never clicked). "not-run": the verb was not asked for or could not start.

details.description: Target-specific facts that no shared code reads. Free-form.

import.description: OPF's importer run on a copy (filled by the round-trip step, absent before).

error.description: The importer's error when status is "failed".

slideCount.description: How many slides the imported deck has.

edit.description: One edit case: one edit made in the application, then one PowerPoint copy written by the application.

id.description: The case's id, safe as a file name: a-z 0-9 . _ - (for example "retype-cell").

what.description: What was edited, one phrase (for example "retyped the text of table cell B2 on slide 3").

path.description: The copy's path relative to this result.json's folder: edits/<id>.pptx.

status.description: The edit and the copy together: "done" when both finished; otherwise as for a verb.

outcomes.description: What every exported object became in this copy (filled by the round-trip step, absent before). Kept here, never merged into the slides' objects, which describe the unedited file.

objects.description: The exported objects whose outcome is not native, in slide order.

name.description: The object's name in the exported file.

outcome.description: What it became in the copy.

how.description: What changed, or why it is gone, one phrase.

kind.description: What the object is. "title": the slide's title placeholder. "body": its body placeholder. "text": other text (a text box, or a shape with text). "list": text with bullets or numbering. "table". "chart". "shape": a shape without text. "connector": a line or connector. "group": a group (its members in objects). "picture": an image. "link": a hyperlink (on text, a shape or a cell). "notes": the slide's presenter notes. "footer": footer text, slide number or date. "diagram": a live SmartArt graphic (layout and node count in details). "media": a video or audio object. A driver that cannot tell a title from other text reports "text".

message.description: What went wrong, in the driver's or the application's words; absent when nothing did.

outcome.description: What the exported object became in the application: "native" (the same kind of editable object), "changed" (editable, but something changed; say what in how), "picture" (a picture of it), "dropped" (gone); null when not determined (a probe alone cannot tell; the round-trip step fills it).

slide.description: One slide of the opened file.

index.description: The slide's position in the file, 1 for the first, hidden slides counted.

hidden.description: True when the slide is hidden (Keynote: skipped).

layout.description: The application's name for the slide's layout (Keynote may add " 0", " 1" to repeated names); null when unknown.

picture.description: The application's picture of the slide, relative to this result.json's folder ("slides/slide-001.png", numbered by index), any pixel size; null when the application exported none (Keynote and LibreOffice skip a hidden slide; PowerPoint exports one), render did not run, or render failed for this slide.

notes.description: The slide's presenter notes as the application reads them; null when it has none or they were not read.

objects.description: The slide's objects in z-order, back to front. Empty when probe did not run.

details.description: Target-specific facts about the slide (for example its placeholders as the application reports them). No shared code reads it.

compare.description: The application's picture compared with OPF's preview (filled by the compare step, absent before).

preview.description: OPF's preview picture of the slide, relative to the run directory (the compare step copies it to preview/<deck>/slide-<n>.png there); null when OPF has no preview of the slide (a hidden slide: OPF previews visible slides only, even when the application exported a picture of it).

score.description: Share of pixels that differ (0 = none); null when there was no pair to compare. A score ranks slides; it is not a verdict.

note.description: Why there was no pair to compare (score null): a hidden slide, no application picture, no preview picture.

aspectDiffers.description: True when the two pictures' aspect ratios differ by more than 0.01 (the application's slide size is not the preview's).

box.description: [x0, y0, x1, y1] as fractions of the slide's width and height.

cells.description: How many grid cells the area covers.

share.description: The area's share of all differing cells.

object.description: One object on a slide, in the shared vocabulary.

how.description: For outcome "changed": what changed, one phrase (for example "split into a group: the shape plus a separate text box").

name.description: The object's name in the file (OPF names its shapes and applications keep them); absent when the application does not expose names.

alt.description: The object's alt text (DrawingML's description, PowerPoint's AlternativeText) as the application holds it; absent when it has none or does not expose it. Compared across applications (opf#1479).

appClass.description: The application's own class name for the object (Keynote: "text item", "shape", "image", "chart", "line", "group", "table"; PowerPoint: its MsoShapeType name).

box.description: [x, y, width, height] in points, slide coordinates, origin at the top left; a group's members too (never relative to their group).

text.description: The object's plain text, cut to at most 200 characters.

fonts.description: The font names the application reports for the object's text, each once, in order of first use.

rows.description: Kind table: the number of rows.

columns.description: Kind table: the number of columns.

role.description: Kind footer: which piece of furniture it is.

on.description: Kind link: what carries the link.

target.description: Kind link: where it goes, a URL or "slide:<index>".

objects.description: Kind group: the group's members, back to front.

details.description: Target-specific facts about the object that no shared code reads (kind diagram: layout and nodes).
